reconstructed_theorem_text: For all natural numbers d,n with 3<=n and n<=d, every real kappa with 4<=kappa, and every family O of real orthogonal n by n matrices indexed by Fin(d div n), define A as follows. Put q = d div n and r = d mod n, with natural-number division and remainder, so d = q*n + r. For each j in {0,...,q-1}, define the real n by n block B_j = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O_j + O_j^T). The resulting real d by d matrix A has q consecutive blocks B_0,...,B_(q-1), followed by I_r, and all entries between distinct blocks or between a main block and the tail are zero. The pair (i,j), with inner coordinate i in {0,...,n-1} and block index j in {0,...,q-1}, maps to coordinate j*n+i. Tail coordinate k in {0,...,r-1} maps to q*n+k. Both row and column indices use this same map (reindexing uses its inverse to retrieve the original entries). If r=0, the tail is empty: I_0 has no entries and adds no coordinates. Then A is symmetric, and for every vector x in R^d, ||x||_2^2 <= x^T A x <= kappa ||x||_2^2, where ||x||_2^2 = sum_(i=0)^(d-1) x_i^2. Both inequalities hold for each x for this same A.
objects: Natural numbers d,n; real scalar kappa; q=d div n; r=d mod n; an indexed family O_j of real orthogonal n by n matrices; blocks B_j; the reindexed real matrix A; identity matrices I_n and I_r; the coordinate equivalence e from ((Fin n x Fin q) disjoint-union Fin r) to Fin d. A real vector x indexed by Fin d; its squared Euclidean norm; the quadratic form x^T A x.
domains: d,n belong to the natural numbers, including zero where not otherwise restricted; kappa belongs to the real numbers; j belongs to Fin q; inner coordinates belong to Fin n; residual coordinates belong to Fin r; A has rows and columns in Fin d and real entries; O maps Fin q to the real orthogonal group on Fin n. x ranges over all functions Fin d -> real, equivalently R^d.
quantifiers: For every d,n : natural numbers, if 3<=n and n<=d, then for every kappa : real, if 4<=kappa, then for every orthogonal family O, let A be the displayed matrix; A is symmetric and for every x : Fin d -> real the lower and upper quadratic inequalities both hold.
assumptions: 3<=n; n<=d; 4<=kappa; O_j is a real orthogonal n by n matrix for every j in Fin(d div n). No randomness, independence, determinant condition, or further relation between the O_j is assumed.
conclusion: A^T=A and, for every x in R^d, ||x||_2^2 <= x^T A x and x^T A x <= kappa*||x||_2^2.
scopes: The matrix blocks are ordered by j first and inner coordinate i second: global coordinate j*n+i; the residual tail starts at q*n. The coordinate equivalence is used for both rows and columns. An empty residual set contributes no identity coordinates. A is locally defined after d,n,kappa,O and is fixed while x ranges over all real d-dimensional vectors. The symmetry assertion is conjoined with the universally quantified pair of inequalities.
constant_dependencies: The dimension hypotheses use 3 and the parameter bound uses 4. The lower quadratic bound has coefficient 1 and the upper bound has coefficient kappa. Block coefficients are exactly (kappa+1)/2 and (kappa-1)/4, with a unit identity residual block. No universal unspecified constant, asymptotic bound, or existential choice appears.
